note: Lesson is almost entirely the خرب / خرّب pair (past, present, command, feminine, plural, food sense) plus the N-verb recap at the end. Many of his Arabic lines between 18:14 and 36:00 are untranscribed ([speaking Arabic]), so A11, A12, A16 and D2 rest on Amal's recasts and his own English asides. Her 25:57 line also came out as 'rose راح يخرب' (engine dropped her el- too), which is why D6 is dropped. D3 (بزعوج) is a vowel-length slip (F2 / S4) - if the merger wants it shown as an F-family card, the moment is 58:50 / 58:53. No added rows.

row.medi_said: Review. What was the word for review? ... What is the word for review?
row.amal_said: As a noun it's مراجعة. So what's-- what is it as a verb? ... صح، براجع.
row.why: Didn't-know: he asked twice for the word for review (02:21, 02:32); she gave the noun مراجعة, asked for the verb, said صح to his مراجعة and supplied براجع herself - one supplied word, not a wrong form (sheet: review | Muraaja3a | مراجعة; i review | Ana baraaje3 | أنا براجع).

rulings.why: Same moment as r2's row; the transcript supports tier 0 (asked), not tier 2: he never produced a wrong form, he repeated the noun she had just given and she said صح before supplying the verb - that is still her supplying a word he did not know. He then used نراجع right at 02:50.

row.medi_said: Oh, but yeah, but [speaking Arabic] and then it's becha... ... Uh, but [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]
row.why: For 'everything she uses' he used the you-feminine form (bitsta3mli); Amal recast بتستعمل at 20:58 and again at 21:13 and he said 'that's right, it's she and not you' at 21:19 - his own words show the person slip though the engine did not write his Arabic.

rulings.why: Real and distinct from A11 (plural بيخربوا) and A12 (missing object ending at 21:19): two recasts of بتستعمل plus his 'it's she and not you' prove he had the 2nd-person feminine form; medium only because his Arabic is untranscribed.

S4 / F2 vowel length, not vocab: he said baz3ooj / banz3ooj (long -oo-) at 58:50, Amal echoed بنزعج, and in his very next line (58:54) he had the right shape himself ('banzaj and bazaj') with the right meanings, and she said ممتاز. The root and the word are right; only the vowel length slipped - sound shape (F family) is not scored as vocab.

Not an error: seconds earlier (49:52-50:17) Amal explained that akle = the one dish you are working on and akel = food in general, and that both are 'food' in English; 'don't ruin my food' in a cooking context fits أكلتي (akleti, my dish) as well as أكلي, and she accepted it (Mm-hmm) and moved on. Nothing in the transcript shows he chose the wrong one.

row.why: She asked where the b- goes ('To the beginning ... of it'); he answered bare أول الكلمة with no preposition; her reply reads as لأول الكلمة (la- 'to', engine split as لا، أول - a plain 'no' before the same words makes no sense) and he at once took it as 'لأول الـ-- في أول الكلمة', which she accepted (mm-hmm). Low because the engine's لا could still be 'no'.
row.english: to the beginning of the word

rulings.why: Her line cannot be 'no' followed by the identical phrase, so it is a recast adding the preposition, and his instant لأول shows he heard it that way; a real but weak D1 row - kept at low confidence.

Cannot be verified - engine: he said الرز at 24:38 and الروز at 25:36 (el- present both times); at 25:57 the engine wrote Amal's own sentence as 'rose راح يخرب' with no el- either, so the dropped el- at 26:04 is the engine's rendering of this word, not evidence of his slip; she answered ممتاز.

row.medi_said: الشمال روس بيكون ... برد كتير ويكون بيمطر أو بتثلج.
row.why: Habitual present about the north of Russia: his first بيكون (06:02) had the b-, the second (ويكون, 06:09) lost it with no modal or time word before it to drop it; Amal let it pass; low because 'وبيكون' can be misheard as 'ويكون' by the engine.

rulings.why: Only r2 saw it; the transcript shows the b- present on the first bikoon and missing on the second with nothing to license the drop, so it is a real but unproven grammar-B (she gave no signal); filed under B1 (present b-) with B8 as the ykoon context, kept low.

challenges.why: بنعيد vs بنزيد differ by one root letter (ع for ز) in the middle of a sound-letter drill (بـ aim الـ an); this may be an S4 root-letter slip rather than the lexical item 'repeat' for 'add' - he said بنعيد again at 11:47 after her بزيد, then بزيد at 11:55, so an audio check should decide whether he meant the wrong word or just mis-sounded it.
